highlights.title: What if Man City's Premier League titles and trophies are stripped?
highlights.summary: Jamie Carragher has called for Manchester City to be stripped of their titles after the club was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules – so what would change?
body: An independent commission found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, during which the club won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield.

Sanctions will be addressed in a further hearing with the independent commission and Man City, who continue to deny the breaches, have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday, October 2 to do so.
Possible sanctions include points deductions, fines, transfer bans and expulsion from the Premier League - but what if City are stripped of their titles and trophies?

They pipped Manchester United on the final day of the season in 2012 through Sergio Aguero's famous winner, then they won the league by two points over Liverpool in 2014 before setting a new record in 2018 by amassing 100 points to deny United again.

highlights.title: All the latest news on Meta’s cute, creepy Muse AI agent
highlights.summary: Meta launched a new Muse AI agent it claims can help you with everything from firing off emails to buying stuff online. Muse can be surprisingly effective at delivering on those promises — if you’re willing to trust Meta with your data and hand Muse your credit card.
body: Tech YouTuber Matt Robb says that Muse gave out his home address to a total stranger this weekend, after authorizing the bot to handle his Facebook Marketplace account. That’s despite Meta placing great emphasis on the security features of Muse when it launched the personal AI agent earlier this month as it tries to catch up with competing AI providers like Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Just found out it told people my address and agreed a lowball price and then they showed up without it even telling me until late tonight that it messed up,” Robb said on Threads, providing a screenshot of Muse’s admission. “[Muse] didn’t tell me any of this until after the guy had left (luckily I’m in an apartment with security),” he added in a follow up post.

Meta says in a blog post today that Muse can now connect to more productivity apps, which it’s pitching as a way to make the agent more helpful for small businesses. Muse has already been able to connect to apps like Gmail and Outlook, but now the list includes Asana, Box, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, Notion, Slack, Stripe, Zoom, and more. Meta also says that Muse will be able to access Facebook and Instagram business accounts.
points: Meta launched a new Muse AI agent it claims can help you with everything from firing off emails to buying stuff online.
Muse can be surprisingly effective at delivering on those promises — if you’re willing to trust Meta with your data and hand Muse your credit card.

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.title: My mother’s phone calls became stranger, but I couldn’t visit. A rescue dog helped me reach her
highlights.summary: Conversation was difficult. But Sally, a dear old German shepherd, gave me a glimpse of my mother’s emotional state. My mother had been wanting a dog for years. She lived in Perth, on the other side of the country to her children and grandchildren who were all grown up.
body: What I didn’t know was that the forbidding fence he was building, the gate operated by keypad and code, wasn’t just to contain a dog. It was to contain my mother.

Dogs became scarce during the Covid pandemic. There wasn’t much on offer at the local pound. In the winter of 2020, my mother and stepfather drove for several hours to collect Sally from a rescue shelter in a distant town. She was a chunky, ageing German shepherd, perhaps 10 or 11, with dense black fur and a grey muzzle, hard of hearing and stiff in the hips. Sally had been let go from a farm as she could no longer jump into the back of the ute. My stepfather lifted her on to a picnic blanket on the backseat of the car and they drove her home.
A few days later I rang my mother to ask about the new dog. “It’s a little yellow puppy,” she said. “It’s very naughty, but it might be better when its tapes have been tied.”

highlights.title: So what's happening with Russia's new, long-delayed crewed spacecraft?
highlights.summary: In what seems like an alternate universe in hindsight, Russia and the European Space Agency began discussing collaboration on next-generation crewed spacecraft two decades ago. Under the agreement, Europe would have provided a service module to power a crew capsule carrying up to six passengers.
body: Beyond the name changes and a flood of renderings, after nearly 20 years of work, then, is anything actually happening with the Eagle spacecraft?

For starters, the relatively new chief executive of Roscosmos, Dmitry Bakanov, appears to have jettisoned the “Eagle” name of the spacecraft favored by Rogozin. In a recently published Interfax story, the spacecraft is referred to as PTK NP.
Bakanov, in comments translated for Ars by Rob Mitchell, told the publication that tests of the spacecraft’s parachute system will begin this fall.
“The first step is the launch and testing of a new, promising, reusable manned transport spacecraft,” he said. “And in the fall, there will be a parachute drop and testing in the Far East.”

highlights.title: MIT Transit Lab to develop an AI platform for public transit agencies
highlights.summary: With $2.1 million funding from Google.org, the open-source Public Transit Intelligence Hub will unify public transit monitoring, operations, and passenger communication.
body: Google.org announced on Sept. 15 that the MIT Transit Lab is a recipient of $2.1 million in funding — one of only 15 projects selected in the worldwide Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. The funding from Google’s philanthropic arm will support NGOs, social enterprises, and academic institutions as they integrate artificial intelligence-powered solutions across topics like health, resilience, and economy.

The Transit Lab’s winning project, the Public Transit Intelligence Hub (PTIQ), aims to unify public transportation agencies’ real-time monitoring, operations control, and passenger communication systems into a single centralized AI-orchestrated platform that will allow transit control center staff to make better-informed, on-the-spot decisions, and provide riders with more immediate and accurate information.

highlights.title: Silent Hill: Townfall’s Hardest Boss Is Getting Nerfed
highlights.summary: Just about a week after Silent Hill: Townfall ' s release, developer Screen Burn has released a patch that hopes to address some early technical frustrations with the horror game. What's more exciting, however, is the reveal that a fix is in the works for one of the game's most frustrating parts.
body: If you've been playing Townfall, The Weight has likely been the bane of your existence. The creature periodically terrorizes protagonist Simon Ordell throughout the foggy town of St. Amelia, but is basically indestructible. That's because [ Warning: slight spoilers ahead.] The Weight is Townfall 's climactic final boss. The encounter, as it currently exists, is simply miserable. The Weight is a damage sponge, and the intermittent appearance of normal enemies during the fight makes the encounter exhausting.

The developer announced Patch 1.3.1 in a post on X. The patch itself improves stuttering issues on PC. Screen Burn also revealed that "We've heard you on struggles with The Weight — gameplay balancing on it's way asap." (Nobody tell them that there's a typo in that sentence, just be grateful a fix is coming.) There is no release date for the update yet, though hopefully it won't be long.

highlights.title: BBC removes article linking bare nails trend to ‘white supremacist standards of beauty’
highlights.summary: Corporation says story did not meet editorial standards after it attracts criticism from US and UK media. A BBC article that included a claim that a trend for bare nails was linked to “white supremacist standards of beauty” has been permanently removed from its website, after editors concluded it…
body: The article, which first ran on the BBC’s website on 27 September, examined an apparent “viral craze” for bare rather than decorated nails. It said the trend had been flooding social media and fashion catwalks.
It also covered criticisms of the trend, which suggested it could “stigmatise bold manicures”. The article noted that nail art had its roots in black, Latino and Asian communities.

In an early section of the article, it quoted the beauty journalist Kristina Rodulfo as saying: “That trend really promotes blankness and this kind of sameness and erasure of culture and identity that is so important to black and brown communities.
“They are often called elegant or tasteful and these are often usually euphemisms that perpetuate white supremacist standards of beauty.”

highlights.title: Introducing SynthID Bio
highlights.summary: Proof of concept for watermarking AI-generated proteins while preserving biological function.
body: Today, we’re introducing SynthID Bio to bring watermarking technology to synthetic biology. SynthID Bio embeds an imperceptible signature directly into the biological code, ensuring the watermark is verifiable not just on a digital model but on the synthesized, physical protein itself – all while preserving its biological function in laboratory testing.

Generative AI is helping scientists address critical biological challenges, from predicting the structure of proteins ( AlphaFold ) to designing entirely new proteins ( AlphaProteo, and ProteinMPNN ), and more recently, developing new bacteriophages, viruses that infect bacteria. Yet these tools also present new challenges: novel AI designs can bypass traditional DNA synthesis screening, while mislabeled synthetic 3D structures risk polluting public databases and misleading downstream research.
SynthID Bio is a family of watermarking methods developed specifically for synthetic biology to strengthen biosecurity and scientific integrity.

highlights.title: Who wins the Arc? Jamie Lynch's big-race runner guide
highlights.summary: Our Senior Form Analyst looks ahead to Europe's most prestigious contest, live on Sky Sports Racing on Sunday, and reveals his big-race fancy.
body: Daryz bids to defend his Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe crown at Parislongchamp on Sunday and out Senior Form Analyst Jamie Lynch has provided a runner-by-runner guide to the coveted Group One contest.

This is everything a Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe should be, first and foremost a clash of nations and generations, and not just a defining race but a deciding race, to decide the best around, while a returning champion always adds an extra layer of motivation and invigoration.

Roger Varian's fourth runner in an Arc, after Kingston Hill's fourth in 2014 and Postponed's fifth (as favourite) in 2016, and Defoe was done by stall 18 in 2018. Saddadd isn't rated nor decorated like any of those, but he's still pushing upwards, a master of marginal gains, taking him from a London Gold Cup to a German Group One, and the Grosser Preis von Baden has had a happy habit of readying Arc winners, like Marienbard, Danedream and Torquator Tasso. That was only his first go at the trip, yet he was fastest at stages of both the Tattersalls Gold Cup and the Coral-Eclipse, Group Ones at a mile and a quarter, and the systematic skin-shedding qualifies him as a lively longshot.

Next up, Hunt: Showdown 1896, Crytek's first-person extraction shooter that sends you off to fight mythological monsters. And don't worry if you haven't played the first 1895 games in the series, you'll soon pick it up.

Finally, Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 is available for PS4 and PS5. This third-person shooter with local and online co-op tells the story of what happened to the voxelEarth after the events of the first installment. Brothers from across the world reunite to face an unprecedented threat brought about by an all-new enemy that threatens to tear the Earth apart all over again.

highlights.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: now is the perfect time to flash some lace
highlights.summary: What you need to lift your autumn wardrobe is something flimsy, flirty and unconventional. At this time of year, my job is mostly banging on about jumpers. Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness and merino sweaters, as Keats would surely have written had he been on Substack.
body: I can worship at the altar of cashmere with the best of them. I can extol the virtues of a sweater in tones normally reserved for fine wines and newborn babies. But today I have a rather different proposition for your autumn wardrobe. The best fillip for your shoulder-season style is not a thick layer, but the opposite. What you need to lift your look right now is something flimsy, flirty, with an edging of lace. A sorbet-coloured lace-edged tank top that is virtually a camisole. A slinky black slip skirt with a lace hem. Something with a frill, that has the thrill of lingerie.

Not on its own, obviously, or you will catch your death. You are going to wear your lacy little whatnot and then you are going to partly cover it up by wearing something on top, and this is the whole point.

highlights.title: ‘Xbox is not for sale’ says Microsoft’s gaming chief
highlights.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports that Microsoft is considering selling off its Xbox business. The Information reported in June that Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood had been considering spinning out Xbox entirely, and then reported earlier this month that both execs have "more…
body: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is taking a ‘long-term view’ of Microsoft’s gaming division.

“Xbox is not for sale,” says Sharma in an interview with The New York Times. “We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model and everything needed to achieve that.”

It appears that Nadella and Hood have favored the giant Xbox “reset” as the plan for Microsoft’s gaming unit instead of making Xbox a joint venture or spinning out the gaming business entirely. Sharma announced her Xbox restructuring in June, calling it a reset for the division. A new AI system that excels at challenging games with hidden information could someday help human decision-makers select ideal strategies to outfox opponents in complicated situations like military maneuvers.

Using advances in machine-learning, researchers from MIT, Carnegie Mellon University, New York University, and Stanford University developed an AI that defeated top-ranked human players of the board wargame Stratego by a large margin — something no AI system had been able to achieve.

Stratego, a two-player game of imperfect information, in which the opponent’s piece identities remain hidden, is often used as a benchmark to test the strategic thinking abilities of powerful AI models.

highlights.title: Google's early attempt to pay websites for AI answers is struggling
highlights.summary: Google's shift to AI-powered search has upended the way the world's largest search engine generates web traffic, rankling large and small publishers alike. In recent months, the company has experimented with paying publishers when their content appears in AI answers, but a new report claims the…
body: According to The Information, Google has admitted about 100 publishers to the AI contribution pilot. The pitch is that websites can get payments from Google when their content materially contributes to Gemini-powered search results like an AI Overview. Google has long resisted the idea of direct payments to publishers, arguing that websites get traffic in exchange for allowing Google bots to scrape their content for use in search and knowledge graph tools. In the age of AI, that relationship is breaking down, hence the AI pilot.

So far, publishers aren't getting much for their trouble. The Information heard from several small and mid-sized publishers in the program that Google's AI payments are minuscule, equaling roughly one-tenth of one percent of their advertising revenue. These payments have been so disappointing that several larger publishers have reportedly declined to participate in the program. These publishers hope that by refusing to join the pilot, they can force Google to offer a more generous deal.

highlights.title: ‘We don’t need boos’: Astros players frustrated as own fans turn on them in playoffs
highlights.summary: Houston announce crowd of 34,011 for playoff opener. Players criticize boos during 6-3 defeat by White Sox. Astros are first division winner with.500 or worse mark. The crowd at Daikin Park was surprisingly sparse as the Houston Astros – baseball’s first division winner with a.500 or worse record …
body: Large swaths of seats, especially in the upper deck, sat empty while right-hander AJ Blumbaugh delivered the game’s first pitch at 4.10pm. The bottom two levels were much fuller than the upper deck, but many seats in the lower two decks were also empty.
The announced attendance was 34,011, in a park with a capacity of 40,963.

All those empty seats are a rare sight in a stadium that is normally packed for the postseason. And some of the fans that did show up weren’t too happy with the performance of the home team with boos raining down on the Astros in the first and second innings as they fell behind 3-0.

“It’s extremely frustrating as a home player,” first baseman Christian Walker told the Athletic. “We’re here, playing at home; we need cheers. We need energy. We don’t need boos. What purpose does that serve in that moment? Whatever fans are feeling, we’re feeling it tenfold. We’re the ones out there. We’re the ones in the fight. We worked our butts off this whole season to put ourselves in this spot, and for guys to get booed, it’s frustrating.”

highlights.title: Geoffrey Rush Has an Idea for How Barbossa Can Return in Pirates of the Caribbean 6
highlights.summary: Pirates of the Caribbean actor Geoffrey Rush has said he's keen to make a return to Disney's swashbuckling franchise, if only to "annoy Jack Sparrow" one last time. Rush is one of just three actors to appear in all five Pirates of the Caribbean movies, alongside Johnny Depp's Captain Jack Sparrow…
body: Of course, Rush's character Hector Barbossa died in the finale of 2016's Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, the franchise's final film to date. But even this would not necessarily stop him from returning, Rush believes.

"There's been a big enough break," Rush told Entertainment Weekly, discussing his desire to return. "I said, you know, I sacrificed myself for my daughter, I don't want it to be too easy and too cheesy that I come back and go: 'give me another payday.' I respect the scale of the opera that's almost been created in that 20 year period.

"I liken it to... Shakespeare," Rush continued, "and Hamlet's father coming back as a ghost. I thought, that would take good writing but just to come back and annoy Jack Sparrow for one more go. I'd even say, get the fans to write in what they'd like to see happen."
